steps.description: On the raw integer gene-level count matrix (12000 genes x 6 samples: 3 treated, 3 control), apply a minimal low-count pre-filter keeping genes with at least 5 counts in at least 3 samples (the smallest group size), lowered from the usual 10-count floor because this is a 3' tag-seq library where long genes collect fewer reads at equal depth. plan.title: Liver treated vs control DESeq2 DE + Hallmark GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative: This is a 3' QuantSeq (Lexogen FWD) tag-seq liver dataset with 3 treated vs 3 control samples, single batch, raw STAR/featureCounts gene-level integer counts (12000 genes x 6 samples). Because the library reads only the 3' end of each transcript, gene counts do not scale with transcript length, so no length-based normalization (TPM/FPKM/tximport) is applied at any step. The plan runs: (1) sample-structure QC (blind VST, PCA, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes) plus a strandedness check, since the metadata declares FWD stranding but no read-level check confirms it; (2) a DESeq2 differential expression step - minimal low-count pre-filter (floor of 5 counts, lowered from the usual 10 because 3' tag counts run lower for long genes), median-of-ratios normalization with a GC-bias diagnostic (no length-bias check needed for 3' data), an explicit reference level (control) and Wald test, apeglm shrinkage of the reported log2FC, and BH-adjusted independent filtering at alpha 0.05; (3) fgsea preranked GSEA on the DESeq2 Wald statistic against MSigDB Hallmark (2026.1, human) and Reactome pathway gene sets, both available in the reference store; (4) a report step consolidating the DE gene table, fit diagnostics, and enrichment results with the reproducibility record. With only 3 replicates per group, the design has limited power for small effects; this caution is carried through the DE and report steps per the grounded procedure, and the significance threshold is not loosened to compensate.
